rfi.description: A leading group monitoring and providing aid to migrants crossing the Mediterranean have warned that its rescue ships have been facing increasing threats and harassment from Libyan groups.

rfi.title: Malian PM's visit to Algeria underlines need for mutual security goals
rfi.description: The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

rfi.title: Six million Somalis face acute hunger as drought and conflict worsen
rfi.description: Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world’s worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".

rfi.title: Violence against healthcare workers in DRC hampers Ebola response
rfi.description: Healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been coming under attack, the United Nations and Red Cross have warned, hampering efforts to stem the spread of the Ebola virus, which is spreading 'exponentially'.

rfi.title: France gathers Ukraine's allies to boost resistance to Russia
rfi.description: Countries allied with Ukraine in its war with Russia are meeting on Monday to reaffirm support for Kyiv and discuss how to pressure Moscow to halt its invasion, in talks held symbolically on Ukraine's independence day. French President Emmanuel Macron will co-chair the gathering of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing" via video link.

rfi.title: Centre-left Glucksmann enters French presidential race as left tries to unite
rfi.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann has announced his candidacy for next year's presidential election, seeking to challenge hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon to lead France's fractured left, as a campaign increasingly dominated by the far right takes shape.

rfi.title: Scorching summer takes toll on bees and honey harvests in France
rfi.description: France produces 20,000 tonnes of honey each year, but successive heatwaves and persistent drought across Europe this summer are impacting bee populations as flowering plants dry out and colonies struggle to find food. Beekeeper Romain Lacotte and his family farm 1,000 hives in Haute-Corrèze, central France, an area considered one of the country's natural water towers. But even there, he tells RFI, high temperatures and lack of rain are taking their toll.

rfi.title: DRC and M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace in eastern Congo
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

rfi.title: Saudi crown prince heads to France as Paris seeks closer Gulf ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day official visit, as Paris looks to deepen ties with Riyadh against a backdrop of war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Mystery elephant deaths in Kenya leave experts divided over cause
rfi.description: Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

rfi.title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French journalists
rfi.description: Togo's government says it has "serious and consistent evidence" against two French documentary filmmakers detained since July on charges of making false statements. Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani were arrested along with their Togolese fixer, Fred Vedomey, and have denied wrongdoing.

rfi.title: Southern African mothers plead for sons lured to Russia's war in Ukraine
rfi.description: Instead of celebrating her son's birthday this month, Zimbabwean mother Rodwin Chitewere spent the day praying for his body to be brought home from Russia, where he was reportedly killed fighting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

rfi.title: 'Niu Lai', the 'so bad it's good' Chinese cartoon becoming a box-office hit
rfi.description: An amateur animated film has become a surprise box-office hit in China, fuelling a wider debate about cinema, artificial intelligence and audience tastes. Made by a mother-and-son team on a shoestring budget, Niu Lai went from commercial failure to viral sensation after attracting a wave of negative reviews.

rfi.title: Eroding coastlines unearth and destroy slave graves in French Caribbean
rfi.description: Rising seas and coastal erosion are exposing the graves of enslaved people on beaches in the French Caribbean departments of Martinique and Guadeloupe, bringing long-buried remains back into view. Archaeologists say the retreating coastline is revealing new information about people who were enslaved centuries ago, but also destroying sites of historical and cultural importance.

rfi.title: France to send interceptor missiles to Ukraine after Russian strikes
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday announced Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles to Ukraine, with Kyiv's air defences running short after the latest round of deadly Russian attacks.

rfi.title: Ravaged by wildfires, France's Fontainebleau forest reopens to public
rfi.description: The forest of Fontainebleau outside Paris has partially reopened to the public after remaining off-limits for over a month due to devastating wildfires. From Saturday, visitors can access some 80 percent of the forest, but are being warned to show caution around fragile wildlife and charred trees.

rfi.title: Diplomats urge France and UK to uphold rule of law in Palestinian territories
rfi.description: Dozens of former senior French and UK diplomats on Saturday urged their governments to work together to uphold international law in the Palestinian territories, accusing Israel of seeking to "destroy" any prospect of a viable Palestinian state.

rfi.title: Still waters run deep: why Palme d'or winner 'Fjord' questions our certainties
rfi.description: An isolated village in Norway sees its peaceful veneer upset by the arrival of a new family in Fjord, the Palme d'Or-winning film released in French cinemas this week. Inspired by real-life cases, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu explores questions of domestic violence, religion, culture and tolerance through a story that asks whose version of the truth can be trusted.

france24fr.description: Une forte sécheresse menace les cultures au Soudan, notamment dans le sud-est du pays.Un nouveau coup dur pour les agriculteurs, alors que la guerre a plongé le pays dans l’une des pires crises alimentaires au monde.

france24fr.title: Près de Paris, l'Arabie saoudite va financer trois parcs d'attractions
france24fr.description: L'Arabie saoudite a signé, lundi, un protocole d'accord avec la France pour créer trois parcs d'attractions en région parisienne, dont l'un probablement sur l'univers des mangas. Le projet d'investissement saoudien de six milliards d'euros, présenté comme "sans précédent" par Emmanuel Macron, doit aussi permettre de créer 22 000 emplois directs.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Les États-Unis dévoilent de nouvelles sanctions visant à "couper toutes les sources de revenus" de l'Iran
Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann veut remporter la primaire socialiste sur une ligne anti-LFI
france24fr.description: Raphaël Glucksmann, désormais candidat à la primaire socialiste, a fait du rapport de la gauche à Jean-Luc Mélenchon et de la question d’une éventuelle alliance avec La France insoumise aux législatives de 2027 un élément central de son projet politique en vue des débats à venir face à ses concurrents.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : le pays fête ses 35 ans d’indépendance malgré la guerre
france24fr.description: L’Ukraine célèbre ce lundi les 35 ans de son indépendance. À Kiev, Volodymyr Zelensky a participé à une cérémonie devant la cathédrale Sainte-Sophie, marquée par une minute de silence en hommage aux soldats morts au combat. Plusieurs dirigeants européens ont également fait le déplacement.

france24fr.title: En RD Congo, une première mission de vérification du cessez-le-feu dans l'Est
france24fr.description: Alors que l'armée congolaise et le groupe politico-militaire AFC/M23, soutenu par le Rwanda, se sont mutuellement accusés d'exactions lundi, une première mission régionale de vérification d'un fragile cessez-le-feu entre les belligérants s'est déployée dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo.

france24fr.title: Coalition des volontaires : comment mieux protéger l’Ukraine ?
france24fr.description: Les alliés de Kiev se réunissent à nouveau au sein de la Coalition des volontaires, alors que les attaques russes contre les civils s’intensifient. Vendredi, une frappe de drones contre un centre commercial a fait 19 morts et 130 blessés. Récit de Dorothée Olliéric (France 2).

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Kiev rassemble ses alliés autour des questions de défense
france24fr.description: Les alliés de Kiev se réunissent à nouveau au sein de la Coalition des volontaires pour renforcer la protection de l’Ukraine face à l’intensification des attaques russes. Décryptage de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Iran : les partenaires de Téhéran dans le viseur de Washington
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis s’apprêtent à annoncer une nouvelle salve de sanctions contre l’Iran, mais aussi contre les pays, entreprises et institutions financières qui continueraient de commercer avec Téhéran. Donald Trump menace ces partenaires de "terribles conséquences économiques", dans le but d’accentuer l’isolement du régime iranien sans engager de nouvelle opération militaire. Correspondance de Sarah Andersen depuis New York pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Guinée : deux ministres proches du président limogés sur fond de lutte anticorruption
france24fr.description: 🇬🇳 En Guinée, deux ministres proches du président Mamadi Doumbouya ont été limogés vendredi. Mory Condé, chargé de l’Emploi, et Mourana Soumah, à la Communication quittent leurs fonctions sans détails sur les motifs de cette décision. Quelques heures plus tard, le chef de l’État a réaffirmé sur Facebook sa volonté de lutter contre la corruption.

france24fr.title: USS Donald Trump ou USS Doris Miller... la Navy va-t-elle effacer le nom d'un héros afro-américain ?
france24fr.description: L'un des prochains porte-avions américain doit porter le nom de Doris Miller, un marin qui s'est illustré lors de l'attaque de Pearl Harbor en décembre 1941. Mais selon plusieurs sources, la Marine envisagerait désormais de le baptiser plutôt du nom du président Donald Trump. Ces révélations suscitent un tollé outre-Atlantique.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : 100 jours après, l'épidémie d'Ebola reste difficile à contenir
france24fr.description: Cent jours après la déclaration officielle de la 17e épidémie d'Ebola en RD Congo, les autorités tentent de freiner la propagation du virus. En l'absence de vaccin contre la souche Boundi Bouguio, la prévention reste essentielle, notamment dans les lieux de travail où se côtoient des personnes venues de différentes régions.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : des ONG alertent sur la montée des discours xénophobes
france24fr.description: Les discours xénophobes se multiplient au Sénégal, notamment sur les réseaux sociaux. Face à la stigmatisation croissante des étrangers, des acteurs de la société civile tirent la sonnette d’alarme.

france24fr.title: "Le Canada ⁠ne sera plus traité comme un État !" : Trump durcit la guerre commerciale contre Ottawa
france24fr.description: Après l'échec des négociations commerciales avec Ottawa, Donald Trump a déclaré, lundi, que les droits ⁠de douane américains ​sur les voitures ou encore l'acier produits au Canada seront portés à 50 % à compter de janvier. Le Premier ministre canadien, Mark Carney, refuse un accord commercial "à n'importe quel prix" avec les États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Macron reçoit MBS à Paris : l’énergie et la défense au cœur des échanges
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron reçoit à Paris le prince héritier saoudien Mohammed ben Salmane pour une journée de discussions diplomatiques et stratégiques. Les deux dirigeants doivent aborder les crises qui traversent le Moyen-Orient : la guerre avec l’Iran, la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz, la situation au Liban et en Syrie, ainsi que le dossier israélo-palestinien. Point d'étape avec Johan Bodin, notre journaliste sur place.

france24fr.title: Mort de Philippe Bouvard : une voix de la radio s’éteint
france24fr.description: Le journaliste, animateur et écrivain Philippe Bouvard est mort ce lundi à l’âge de 96 ans, à son domicile de Cannes. Créateur et animateur historique des Grosses Têtes pendant 37 ans, Philippe Bouvard a marqué durablement la radio et la télévision françaises. Retiré des ondes depuis janvier 2025, il laisse derrière lui une carrière hors norme et plusieurs générations d’auditeurs. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation contre les mutilations génitales féminines à Paris
france24fr.description: Des centaines de personnes ont manifesté ce samedi à Paris pour dire non aux mutilations génitales féminines. Une mobilisation qui intervient après la diffusion d'une campagne pro-excision sur les réseaux sociaux au Mali.

france24fr.title: Iran : une économie exsangue sous la menace de nouvelles sanctions américaines
france24fr.description: L’économie iranienne s’enfonce dans la crise. L’inflation annuelle a atteint 66% en juillet, tandis que les prix à la consommation ont bondi de 87,9% sur un an ; pour l’alimentation, la hausse atteint 128%. Correspondance de Siavosh Ghazi depuis Téhéran.

zeit.description: Norwegen will nicht von seinen Plänen für eine Öl- und Gasförderung in der arktischen Barentssee abrücken. Damit geht das Land auf Konfrontationskurs zur EU.

zeit.description: Im Zentrum der Neuordnung Europas muss künstliche Intelligenz stehen. Das ist bei den Staats- und Regierungschefs noch nicht ausreichend angekommen.

zeit.description: In Plauen fordern zehntausend Menschen den Rücktritt der Bundesregierung. Rechtsextreme wirken dabei an wichtigen Positionen mit. Was steckt hinter dem »Projekt M1llion«?

zeit.title: Balon-Markt in Turin: Lauter Schätze im Gerümpel
zeit.description: In Turins Altstadt gibt es seit dem 19. Jahrhundert einen Flohmarkt. Rundherum haben sich Antiquitätenhändler angesiedelt, die sogar Möbel von Marie Antoinette verkaufen.

zeit.title: Quality Time: So viel Zeit mit ihren Eltern brauchen Kinder wirklich
zeit.description: Ein Kind braucht Zeit mit den Eltern. Doch was, wenn beide Vollzeit arbeiten? Reichen auch Quality-Ausflüge am Wochenende? Wir erklären, was die Wissenschaft dazu weiß.

zeit.description: An Frankreichs Schulen gilt nun in allen Jahrgängen ein Handyverbot – von Grundschule bis Oberstufe. Das Verbot sei zum Schutz der Kinder, sagt Präsident Emmanuel Macron.

spiegel.title: Sebastian Vettel: Ex-Formel-1-Weltmeister will nun das Segeln lernen
spiegel.description: Viermal gewann Sebastian Vettel den Titel als Formel-1-Weltmeister, nach dem Ende seiner Laufbahn wurde er Miteigentümer eines Segelteams. Nun will er den Sport selbst lernen. Der 39-Jährige hat Respekt vor der Aufgabe.

spiegel.description: Enteignen oder Baugesellschaft gründen: Um hohe Mieten zu bekämpfen, rufen Politiker und Aktivisten nach mehr Staat. Helfen könnte ein radikal neuer Ansatz.

spiegel.description: Die USA haben abermals ein Boot im Pazifik angegriffen, dabei wurden zwei mutmaßliche Drogenschmuggler getötet. Die Militäreinsätze sind hochumstritten.

spiegel.title: Pfaffenhofen an der Ilm: Wie ein halbes Brot eine Bäckerei aus Bayern 15.000 Euro kostete

spiegel.description: Vor einem Jahr erst übernahm sie die französische Entsprechung zur »Tagesschau«. Doch nun zieht sich Léa Salamé zurück: Ihr Lebensgefährte Raphaël Glucksmann will Präsident werden, sie kommt Parteilichkeitsvorwürfen zuvor.

letemps.description:
Le journaliste et animateur radio Philippe Bouvard est mort lundi à 96 ans. Créateur de l’émission «Les Grosses Têtes», il a été un pilier de la station RTL

Figure des médias, le journaliste et animateur radio Philippe Bouvard est décédé lundi à l’âge de 96 ans, a annoncé la station RTL, dont il a été un pilier et où il avait créé l’émission «Les Grosses Têtes» il y a près de 50 ans

observador.title: Carlos Coelho: "Ideia de o país não ter OE é ideia perigosa"
observador.description: O presidente da Universidade de Verão do PSD espera que oposição seja responsável para aprovar o OE. Carlos Coelho sai ainda em defesa do Executivo, relativamente ao estudo sobre a segurança social.

observador.title: Regina Duarte "definitivamente não" voltaria à política
observador.description: Mãe e filha atrizes deram uma entrevista conjunta para promover uma peça, mas foi o "tema Bolsonaro" a dominar, com Gabriela a tentar travar as respostas da mãe, sem sucesso.

observador.title: Mau tempo encerra "stands" da Feira do Livro
observador.description: Devido às condições meteorológicas, a autarquia decidiu encerrar a parte comercial do evento, reprogramando as restantes atividades paralelas.

observador.title: MNE confirma morte de portuguesa em incêndio em restaurante
observador.description: O incêndio numa cidade suíça fez quatro mortos e oito feridos na sexta-feira. Entre as vítimas portuguesas: uma morta e dois feridos, um em estado grave.

observador.title: Sismo de magnitude 6 registado perto de Timor-Leste
observador.description: O USGS situou o epicentro a 215 km de Lospalos. A região integra o Anel de Fogo do Pacífico, uma das mais sísmicas do planeta.

observador.title: Detido suspeito de atear pelo menos 5 fogos no Peso da Régua
observador.description: A PJ de Vila Real deteve um homem de 53 anos. A investigação, iniciada a 25 de julho, analisa 15 fogos na zona de Moura Morta com o mesmo método.

observador.title: "Não é possível" verificar acessos a dados do Chega
observador.description: Executivo de Bolieiro responde a requerimento do partido e admite que os sistemas não permitem identificar quem acedeu, quando ou porquê. Chega denuncia situação "grave para a democracia".

observador.title: Ventura acusa Governo de "roubo" nos combustíveis
observador.description: "São 700 milhões de euros a mais do que devíamos cobrar às pessoas". André Ventura afirmou ainda que Portugal continua a aplicar uma taxa ilegal sobre os combustíveis, a da segurança rodoviária.

observador.title: Assaltos a museus são mais violentos e mais caros
observador.description: Assalto ao Louvre é um exemplo da nova natureza dos roubos a museus europeus: mais violentos, com alvos mais valiosos e assaltantes "oportunistas" de um mercado negro para a arte em expansão.

observador.title: Como um procurado por tortura foi psicólogo em escolas
observador.description: Acusado por tortura no Brasil, Djalma Henares fugiu para Portugal e candidatou-se a cerca 30 de concursos públicos. Exerceu em escolas no Alentejo e Cascais. Registo criminal estava limpo.

observador.title: Preventiva para suspeito de esfaquear o pai em Monção
observador.description: O suspeito atacou o pai dentro de casa, em Monção, no sábado. A segunda vítima foi atingida durante a fuga. Ambos foram hospitalizados.

observador.title: Costa debate orçamento e migrações nas capitais europeias
observador.description: Tal como em 2024 e 2025, Costa irá passar por todos os Estados-membros para "recolher as opiniões dos chefes de Estado ou Governo" sobre o próximo orçamento de longo prazo europeu.

observador.title: Sony acaba com os jogos físicos para a PlayStation
observador.description: Sony abandona os suportes físicos a partir de 2028 e passa a vender 'licenças para jogar'. Em reação, um grupo de jogadores já começou uma semana de boicote à plataforma.

observador.title: CGTP exige retirada do subsídio social de desemprego da PSU
observador.description: A central sindical alerta que a integração na Prestação Social Única reduz duração, valor e contribuições registadas para pensão dos desempregados sem acesso ao subsídio de desemprego.

observador.title: Talibãs proíbem por lei todas as manifestações
observador.description: Nova lei policial aprovada pelo líder supremo talibã elimina qualquer enquadramento jurídico para protestos e alarga poderes coercivos das forças de segurança.

observador.title: Papa assinala "momento difícil" do exército português
observador.description: O Papa evocou a parábola do Bom Samaritano para descrever os dois soldados mortos na autoestrada. Uma comitiva de 129 militares e forças de segurança esteve em audiência privada no Vaticano.

observador.title: CP adere ao passe intermodal de Coimbra em outubro
observador.description: A presidente da Câmara de Coimbra confirmou a adesão da CP ao bilhete Move-C na mesma data dos transportes intermunicipais. Em aberto fica o fim do transporte gratuito entre as estações.

Dabei muss in einer freien Gesellschaft auch die kritische Diskussion über den Sozialstaat und sogar über die Demokratie erlaubt sein.

phys-org.description: Temperatures have been off the charts this year in Europe, the continent warming faster than any other continent. Here are five reasons why Europe's summer of 2026 will go down in the history of climate change:

phys-org.title: One step closer to the ideal glass—simulations reveal hidden order at absolute zero
phys-org.description: In the physical sense, glass is not limited to familiar window glass; it forms whenever a liquid is cooled so quickly that it cannot crystallize. As a result, glass has an amorphous structure—that is, its "building blocks" are not arranged regularly as in crystals. At the same time, however, glass is as resistant to deformation as a crystalline solid.

phys-org.title: Cowpea plants create underground defense system for the next generation after insect attacks
phys-org.description: Plants might seem helpless when it comes to insect attacks, but they are known to employ various techniques to deter pests. One of these techniques involves sending out signals to recruit parasitoid wasps, and a new study, published in Cell Reports, has found that at least one plant can extend this deterrent system to future generations growing in the same soil.

phys-org.title: South Africa produces enough food, yet millions face hunger. Better cold storage could help change that
phys-org.description: South Africa can produce enough food for its population, according to official statistics. But millions face hunger, partly because food is lost and wasted in the value chain. An estimated 10.3 million metric tons of food is wasted annually in the country, 19% of it fresh produce.

phys-org.title: Mechanical memory helps explain how cells adapt their movement to changing environments
phys-org.description: Cells in our bodies squeeze through dense tissue channels, thread past neighboring cells and navigate every nook and cranny within the extracellular matrix—the mesh-like network that surrounds and supports cells. How well they do this can shape a wide range of physiological processes, from wound repair to the spread of cancer.

phys-org.title: Corners in focus: Metasurface enables motion tracking without digital image processing
phys-org.description: A research team at City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK) has developed a new optical corner-detection imaging method that uses azimuthal Hilbert transform metasurfaces and is designed to work as a universal framework. The study marks an important advance in high-speed, low-power optical information processing and has demonstrated potential for motion-tracking applications.

phys-org.title: What live sewage spill data does (and doesn't) tell us about water pollution
phys-org.description: During periods of heavy rainfall, pipes known as storm overflows aim to prevent excess water from overflowing into the sewage system. But this is not always the case.

phys-org.title: The world inches toward catastrophic climate events: 'Bigger shocks are on the way'
phys-org.description: In the opening scene of American writer Kim Stanley Robinson's "The Ministry for the Future," a heat wave combined with a breakdown of the electrical grid in India kills 20 million people. The devastation causes the world's nations to unite to combat climate change.

phys-org.title: Listening to the bush: How AI can help NZ rid its wilderness of 'hold‑out' pest possums
phys-org.description: Possums are among New Zealand's most destructive introduced mammals. They damage native forests, prey on wildlife and remain a major target of the country's Predator Free 2050 program.

phys-org.title: Can satellites detect when forests lose resilience?
phys-org.description: For years, scientists have been using a method called "temporal autocorrelation (TAC)" to measure forest resilience using satellite data. However, scientists have not used TAC uniformly, and its use as a resilience indicator was based largely on theories and assumptions rather than direct evidence from observations on the ground.

phys-org.title: Soil bacteria share amino acids, helping nearly half survive nutrient gaps
phys-org.description: Bacteria, too, depend on good neighborly relations: A new study by the Osnabrück University, in collaboration with researchers from the University of Cambridge in England, shows that soil bacteria live in beneficial communities and frequently exchange nutrients with one another. The study, led by Prof. Dr. Christian Kost, has now been published in the journal Nature Microbiology.

phys-org.title: Floating wetlands slash wastewater greenhouse gas emissions, according to study
phys-org.description: A world-first trial of floating wetland pods in wastewater lagoons shows they cut greenhouse gas emissions by more than a quarter, highlighting their potential as a nature-based solution for decarbonizing the water sector.

phys-org.title: Tiny root hairs, big impact: How bacteria help plants survive drought
phys-org.description: What helps plants cope better with drought? With heat waves and periods of extreme drought becoming increasingly common worldwide, the need for drought-tolerant plants is increasingly urgent. With the help of bacteria, plants can unlock traits that help them cope with drought, securing biodiversity and food safety.

phys-org.title: As California embraces universal transitional kindergarten, the state's other child-care workers are struggling
phys-org.description: Last spring, UC Berkeley researcher Anna Powell sat in on a Zoom call as a number of Bay Area child care center leaders discussed, with sympathy and frustration, the difficult position their businesses were in.

phys-org.title: Antarctic bacteria share 'life‑support' genes to survive extreme conditions
phys-org.description: Antarctica is one of the driest, coldest places on Earth. Very little life survives its extremes. In the soils scattered around the frozen ice sheets, however, communities of microbes do survive. And one of the keys to their success is a surprisingly communal strategy.

phys-org.title: A forecast is not a decision: Design engineering for drought preparedness
phys-org.description: More than 80 countries face chronic drought, yet only a third have systems in place to act before a drought arrives rather than after. The gap is costly. According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, every $1 invested in anticipatory action can save up to $7 in averted losses, while also helping protect lives and livelihoods before crisis conditions take hold. Acting early works. So why don't more countries do it?

phys-org.title: Climate scientists solve monsoon puzzle and warn of risks to fisheries
phys-org.description: A new study has reconciled a long-standing paradox in the South Asian summer monsoon cycle. Climate scientists have discovered why geological records from land and sea have told opposite stories about monsoons throughout history and found that rising temperatures over Southern Africa reduce upwelling in the Arabian Sea, which could damage marine productivity and fisheries. The work is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine

One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

proj-syn.title: MDBs Are Becoming a New Global Safe Asset
proj-syn.description: Even as multilateralism faces an existential threat, multilateral development banks are not only surviving but thriving. Thanks to MDBs’ ability to borrow at costs close to that of the US Treasury, they have created a new class of de facto risk-free assets that could help underpin the global financial system.

proj-syn.title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
proj-syn.description: What is the apparent fragility in the US bond market telling us? Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

proj-syn.title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
proj-syn.description: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention. Yet the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Three Ways AI Will Change the Course of Humanity
proj-syn.description: The AI debate has largely focused on productivity gains and job displacement, but its consequences will reach much further By revolutionizing how we combat disease, wage wars, and stimulate income growth, AI could fundamentally alter the terms of human existence.
